name: Restoring Increasing Sequence
description: Peter wrote on the board a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers a 1 , a 2 , ..., a n . Then Vasil replaced some digits in the numbers of this sequence by question marks. Thus, each question mark corresponds to exactly one lost digit. Restore the the original sequence knowing digits remaining on the board.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains integer n ( 1 ≤ n ≤ 10 5 ) — the length of the sequence. Next n lines contain one element of the sequence each. Each element consists only of digits and question marks. No element starts from digit 0 . Each element has length from 1 to 8 characters, inclusive.
output_specification: If the answer exists, print in the first line " YES " (without the quotes). Next n lines must contain the sequence of positive integers — a possible variant of Peter's sequence. The found sequence must be strictly increasing, it must be transformed from the given one by replacing each question mark by a single digit. All numbers on the resulting sequence must be written without leading zeroes. If there are multiple solutions, print any of them. If there is no answer, print a single line " NO " (without the quotes).
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 490E — Restoring Increasing Sequence [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
